'''Bruno Courcelle''' is a French [[mathematician]] and [[computer scientist]], best known for [[Courcelle's theorem]] in [[graph theory]].

==Life==
Courcelle earned his Ph.D. in 1976 from the [[French Institute for Research in Computer Science and Automation]], then called IRIA, under the supervision of [[Maurice Nivat]]. He then joined the Laboratoire Bordelais de Recherche en Informatique (LaBRI) at the [[University of Bordeaux 1]], where he remained for the rest of his career.<ref name="nivat"/> He has been a senior member of the [[Institut Universitaire de France]] since 2007.<ref>[http://iuf.amue.fr/author/bcourcelle/ Bruno Courcelle] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140315055625/http://iuf.amue.fr/author/bcourcelle/ |date=March 15, 2014 }}, [[Institut Universitaire de France]], retrieved 2014-06-24.</ref>

A workshop in honor of  Courcelle's retirement was held in Bordeaux in 2012.<ref name="nivat">[http://bc12.labri.fr/nivat-courcelle.pdf Bruno Courcelle], text of remarks presented by [[Maurice Nivat]] at Courcelle workshop, retrieved 2014-06-24.</ref><ref>[http://bc12.labri.fr/ Bruno's workshop, June 18-20, 2012, LaBRI, Bordeaux], retrieved 2014-06-24.</ref> Courcelle was the first recipient of the [[Computability in Europe#S._Barry_Cooper_Prize|S. Barry Cooper Prize]] of the [[Computability in Europe|Association Computability in Europe]] in 2020.<ref>
{{cite web
 | url = https://www.acie.eu/2020/06/03/2020-s-barry-cooper-prize-awarded-to-bruno-courcelle/

During the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], Courcelle protested against vaccination mandates in France.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Amiel|first=Sandrine|date=2021-07-26|title=Who are France's anti-vaccine rule protesters and what do they want?|url=https://www.euronews.com/2021/07/26/who-are-france-s-anti-vaccine-rule-protesters-and-what-do-they-want|access-date=2021-08-09|website=euronews|language=en}}</ref>

==Work==
He is known for [[Courcelle's theorem]], which combines [[second-order logic]], the theory of [[formal language]]s, and [[tree decomposition|tree decompositions of graphs]] to show that a wide class of algorithmic problems in [[graph theory]] have efficient solutions.

Notable publications also include:
* {{cite journal | author=Bruno Courcelle | title=Fundamental Properties of Infinite Trees | journal=[[Theoretical Computer Science (journal)|Theoretical Computer Science]] | volume=25 | pages=95&ndash;169 | year=1983 | issue=2 | doi=10.1016/0304-3975(83)90059-2 }}
* {{cite book | author=Bruno Courcelle | chapter=Recursive Applicative Program Schemes | pages=459&ndash;492 | isbn=0-444-88074-7 | editor=Jan van Leeuwen | editor-link=Jan van Leeuwen | title=Formal Models and Semantics | publisher=Elsevier | series=Handbook of Theoretical Computer Science | volume=B | year=1990}}    
* {{cite book |doi=10.1007/3-540-48685-2_7 |chapter=Hierarchical Graph Decompositions Defined by Grammars and Logical Formulas |title=Rewriting Techniques and Applications |series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science |date=1999 |last1=Courcelle |first1=Bruno |volume=1631 |pages=90–91 |isbn=978-3-540-66201-3 | publisher=Springer}}
